punchline: In many companies the person who wins a customer gets the bonus and the one who keeps them gets nothing, which Reichheld argues is backwards.
thirty_sec: Frederick Reichheld looked at what a customer costs and brings over time. Winning one is expensive: senior managers get pulled into proposals, and new customers fill the help desk. A loyal customer adds base profit, savings, referrals and a price premium. Yet many companies pay salespeople only for new accounts, not for keeping them.
